Definition: from a compound of G575 and G5258; properly, to become awake, i.e. (by implication) to drop (off) in slumber:--fall asleep.
BiblicalUsage: Once, on the lake. As they sailed, Jesus fell asleep — the word means He dropped off into slumber — and then the storm came down and the boat filled with water, and the disciples were in jeopardy.
TheologicalSignificance: The word is only the quiet before the storm; its weight is that Jesus slept through the wind His own disciples feared.
